prompt: Stage 4-1, level 6, 52 gold, 70 HP, alternating wins and losses. Your six units are all 2-stars (1-, 2- and 3-costs) with three items in play, and you are 12 XP from level 7. At level 6 the shop shows 3-costs 25% and 4-costs 5% per slot; at level 7 it is 43% and 10%. Level to 7, or roll at 6 for the 3-cost upgrades?

options.label: Level to 7 (12 gold), field a seventh unit, and keep 40: roll at 4-2 after the augment only if the board needs it
Stay level 6 and roll 30 gold: the 2-stars are done, so go for a 3-star on the 3-cost carry
Stay level 6 and save to 88 gold so you can jump straight to level 8 at 4-5

explanation:
A full 2-star board of cheap units at 4-1 has done its job; what it needs next is a 4-cost carry or tank, and those come from level 7 and 8 shops. Level 7 doubles 4-cost odds (5% to 10%) and nearly doubles 3-costs (25% to 43%), adds a seventh unit immediately, and costs 12 gold: 52 becomes 40, still 4 interest, and 4-2 (the augment round) is where the level-7 roll happens if the board needs one.

Rolling at level 6 spends 30 gold in a shop that is 70% 1- and 2-costs, and a 3-star 3-cost needs nine copies from a pool of 18 that other players hold too; you would find two copies and be at 22 gold, level 6, at 4-2. Saving to 88 for level 8 means three more stage-4 fights at level 6 against level-7 boards, at 10 to 15 HP a loss; 70 HP does not survive that plan. The standard timing exists because the lobby follows it: 7 at 4-1, 8 around 4-5 or 5-1.
principle: Level 7 at 4-1. A 2-star board of cheap units has no upgrades left at level 6; the upgrades are in the level-7 shop.
commonMistake: Rolling at level 6 on a finished 2-star board, chasing 3-stars in a shop that is mostly 1- and 2-costs.
hint: Compare the 3-cost and 4-cost odds at 6 and 7, then ask what a level-6 shop can still add to a board whose units are all 2-star.
